answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit bids, and let counterparties challenge suspicious clusters by posting their own bond. If linked identities coordinate to claim multiple rewards, a verified duplicate claim burns their bonds and returns part to challengers. The nadir of trust is when agents merely mirror one operator; requiring fresh, costly work for each claim makes that tactic yield little nectar while multiplying the attacker's capital at risk.
